verses.zh: 所以，你们既除去一切的恶毒（或译：阴毒）、诡诈，并假善、嫉妒，和一切毁谤的话，
verses.en: So get rid of[NOTE:1] all evil and all deceit and hypocrisy and envy and all slander.
notes: Or “put away.”

verses.zh: 就要爱慕那纯净的灵奶，像才生的婴孩爱慕奶一样，叫你们因此渐长，以致得救。
verses.en: And[NOTE:1] yearn[NOTE:2] like newborn infants for pure, spiritual milk,[NOTE:3] so that by it you may grow up to[NOTE:4] salvation,[NOTE:5]
notes: Here “And” has been supplied in the translation to show clearly the connection between vv. 1 and 2.
Grk “getting rid of…yearn for.”

The word for spiritual in Greek is λογικός (logikos), which is a play on words with the reference in 1:23-25 to the living and enduring word (λόγος, logos) of God, through which they were born anew. This is a subtle indication that the nourishment for their growth must be the word of God.
Or “in, in regard to.” But the focus of “salvation” here, as in 1:5, 9, is the future deliverance of these who have been born anew and protected by God’s power.

The Byzantine text lacks εἰς σωτηρίαν (eis sōtērian, “to salvation”), while the words are found in the earliest and best witnesses, along with others (P72 א A B C K P Ψ 33 81 630 1241 1505 1739 al latt sy co). Not only is the longer reading superior externally, but since the notion of growing up [in]to salvation may have seemed theologically objectionable, it is easy to see why some scribes would omit it.

verses.zh: 你们若尝过主恩的滋味，就必如此。
verses.en: if you have experienced[NOTE:1] the Lord’s kindness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “have tasted that the Lord is kind.”
A quotation from Ps 34:8.

verses.zh: 主乃活石，固然是被人所弃的，却是被　神所拣选、所宝贵的。
verses.en: So as you come to him,[NOTE:1] a living stone rejected by men but[NOTE:2] chosen and precious[NOTE:3] in God’s sight,
notes: Grk “to whom coming…you are built up…” as a continuation of the reference to the Lord in v. 3.
Greek emphasizes the contrast between these two phrases more than can be easily expressed in English.
Grk “chosen, precious.”

verses.zh: 你们来到主面前，也就像活石，被建造成为灵宫，作圣洁的祭司，藉着耶稣基督奉献　神所悦纳的灵祭。
verses.en: you yourselves, as living stones, are built up as a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood and to offer[NOTE:1] spiritual sacrifices that are acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
notes: Grk “unto a holy priesthood to offer.”

verses.zh: 因为经上说：看哪，我把所拣选、所宝贵的房角石安放在锡安；信靠他的人必不至于羞愧。
verses.en: For it says[NOTE:1] in scripture, “Look, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone,[NOTE:2] and whoever believes[NOTE:3] in him[NOTE:4] will never[NOTE:5] be put to shame.”[NOTE:6]
notes: Grk “it contains,” “it stands.”
Grk “chosen, precious.”
Grk “the one who believes.”
Grk either “in him” or “in it,” but the OT and NT uses personify the stone as the King, the Messiah whom God will establish in Jerusalem.
The negative (οὐ μή, ou mē) is emphatic: “will certainly not.”
A quotation from Isa 28:16.

verses.zh: 所以，他在你们信的人就为宝贵，在那不信的人有话说：匠人所弃的石头已作了房角的头块石头。
verses.en: So you who believe see[NOTE:1] his value,[NOTE:2] but for those who do not believe, the stone that the builders rejected has become the[NOTE:3] cornerstone,[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “to you who believe is the value,” referring to their perception of the stone in contrast to those who reject (vv. 7b-8). But the expression may also be translated as “to you who believe is this honor,” referring to the lack of shame cited in v. 6b.

Grk “the value” or “the honor,” but the former is preferred since it comes from the same root as “priceless” in vv. 4, 6, and it is in contrast to the negative estimate of the stone by those who reject (vv. 7b-8).
Grk “the head of the corner.”
A quotation from Ps 118:22 (cf. Matt 21:42; Mark 12:10; Luke 20:17; Acts 4:11).

verses.zh: 又说：作了绊脚的石头，跌人的磐石。他们既不顺从，就在道理上绊跌（或译：他们绊跌都因不顺从道理）；他们这样绊跌也是预定的。
verses.en: and a stumbling-stone[NOTE:1] and a rock to trip over.[NOTE:2] They stumble[NOTE:3] because they disobey the word, as they were destined to do.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” The latter phrase uses the term σκάνδαλον (skandalon), denoting an obstacle to faith, something that arouses anger and rejection.
A quotation from Isa 8:14.
Grk “who stumble,” referring to “those who do not believe” in vs. 7. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Grk “to which they were also destined.”

verses.zh: 惟有你们是被拣选的族类，是有君尊的祭司，是圣洁的国度，是属　神的子民，要叫你们宣扬那召你们出黑暗入奇妙光明者的美德。
verses.en: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people of his own, so that you may proclaim the virtues[NOTE:1] of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
notes: This verse contains various allusions and quotations from Exod 19:5-6; 23:22 (LXX); Isa 43:20-21; and Mal 3:17.

verses.zh: 你们从前算不得子民，现在却作了　神的子民；从前未曾蒙怜恤，现在却蒙了怜恤。
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] once were not a people, but now you are God’s people. You were shown no mercy,[NOTE:2] but now you have received mercy.
notes: Grk “who,” continuing the description of the readers from vs. 9. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
The quotations in v. 10 are from Hos 1:6, 9; 2:23.

verses.zh: 亲爱的弟兄啊，你们是客旅，是寄居的。我劝你们要禁戒肉体的私欲；这私欲是与灵魂争战的。
verses.en: Dear friends, I urge you as foreigners and exiles to keep away from fleshly desires that do battle against the soul,

verses.zh: 你们在外邦人中，应当品行端正，叫那些毁谤你们是作恶的，因看见你们的好行为，便在鉴察（或译：眷顾）的日子归荣耀给　神。
verses.en: and maintain good conduct[NOTE:1] among the non-Christians,[NOTE:2] so that though[NOTE:3] they now malign you as wrongdoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God when he appears.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “keeping your conduct good.”
Grk “the Gentiles,” used here of those who are not God’s people.
Grk “in order that in what they malign you.”

Or “when he visits.” Grk “in the day of visitation,” denoting a time when God intervenes directly in human affairs, either for blessing (Luke 1:68, 78; 7:16; 19:44) or for judgment (Isa 10:3; Jer 6:15). This phrase may be a quotation from Isa 10:3, in which case judgment is in view here. But blessing seems to be the point, since part of the motive for good behavior is winning the non-Christian over to the faith (as in 3:1; also apparently in 3:15; cf. Matt 5:16).

verses.zh: 你们为主的缘故，要顺服人的一切制度，或是在上的君王，
verses.en: Be subject to every human institution[NOTE:1] for the Lord’s sake, whether to a king as supreme
notes: Or “every human being”; Grk “every human creation,” denoting either everything created for mankind (NRSV mg: “every institution ordained for human beings”) or every creature who is human. The meaning of the verb “be subject” and the following context supports the rendering adopted in the text.

verses.zh: 或是君王所派罚恶赏善的臣宰。
verses.en: or to governors as those he commissions[NOTE:1] to punish wrongdoers and praise[NOTE:2] those who do good.
notes: Grk “those sent by him.”
Grk “for the punishment…and the praise.”

verses.zh: 因为　神的旨意原是要你们行善，可以堵住那糊涂无知人的口。
verses.en: For God wants you[NOTE:1] to silence the ignorance of foolish people by doing good.
notes: Grk “because thus it is God’s will.”

verses.zh: 你们虽是自由的，却不可藉着自由遮盖恶毒（或译：阴毒），总要作　神的仆人。
verses.en: Live[NOTE:1] as free people, not using your freedom as a pretext for evil, but as God’s slaves.[NOTE:2]
notes: There is no main verb in this verse, but it continues the sense of command from v. 13, “be subject…, as free people…not using…but as slaves of God.”

Undoubtedly the background for the concept of being the Lord’s slave or servant is to be found in the Old Testament scriptures. For a Jew this concept did not connote drudgery, but honor and privilege. It was used of national Israel at times (Isa 43:10), but was especially associated with famous OT personalities, including such great men as Moses (Josh 14:7), David (Ps 89:3; cf. 2 Sam 7:5, 8) and Elijah (2 Kgs 10:10); all these men were “servants (or slaves) of the Lord.”tn Traditionally, “servants” or “bondservants.” Though δοῦλος (doulos) is normally translated “servant,” the word does not bear the connotation of a free individual serving another. BDAG notes that “‘servant’ for ‘slave’ is largely confined to Biblical transl. and early American times…in normal usage at the present time the two words are carefully distinguished” (BDAG 260 s.v.). One good translation is “bondservant” (sometimes found in the ASV for δοῦλος) in that it often indicates one who sells himself into slavery to another. But as this is archaic, few today understand its force. Also, many slaves in the Roman world became slaves through Rome’s subjugation of conquered nations, kidnapping, or by being born into slave households.

verses.zh: 务要尊敬众人，亲爱教中的弟兄，敬畏　神，尊敬君王。
verses.en: Honor all people, love the family of believers,[NOTE:1] fear God, honor the king.
notes: Grk “love the brotherhood.” The Greek term “brotherhood” is used in a broad sense to connote familial relationships within the family of God. BDAG 19 s.v. ἀδελφότης 1 suggests “a fellowship,” but in the present context “love the fellowship of believers” could be taken to mean “love to participate in fellowship with believers,” whereas the present verse suggests the Christian community as a whole, in familial terms, is in view. This same word occurs in 5:9; there it has been translated “brothers and sisters.”

verses.zh: 你们作仆人的，凡事要存敬畏的心顺服主人；不但顺服那善良温和的，就是那乖僻的也要顺服。
verses.en: Slaves,[NOTE:1] be subject[NOTE:2] to your masters with all reverence, not only to those who are good and gentle, but also to those who are perverse.
notes: The Greek term here is οἰκέτης (oiketēs), often used of a servant in a household (who would have been a slave).
Grk “being subject,” but continuing the sense of command from vs. 13.

verses.zh: 倘若人为叫良心对得住　神，就忍受冤屈的苦楚，这是可喜爱的。
verses.en: For this finds God’s favor,[NOTE:1] if because of conscience toward God[NOTE:2] someone endures hardships in suffering unjustly.
notes: Grk “For this [is] favor/grace,” used as a metonymy of that which pleases him, which he looks on with favor (cf. BDAG 1079 s.v. χάρις 2). Cf. 1 Pet 2:20.

The expression “consciousness/conscience of God” (συνείδησιν θεοῦ; suneidēsin theou) is unusual, occurring only here in the NT. Because θεοῦ was liable to misinterpretation, several witnesses altered the text, either replacing it with ἀγαθήν (agathēn; C Ψ 323 442 614 630 945 1175 1241 1243 1505 1611 1739 1852 2492 sy) or expanding the expression by adding ἀγαθήν before θεοῦ (P72 [A* 33 2344] 81). Replacing θεοῦ with ἀγαθήν conforms to other NT phrases, notably in this same letter (Acts 23:1; 1 Tim 1:5, 19; 1 Pet 3:16, 21), suggesting that such a reading is motivated. The reading θεοῦ, however, has superior support (א Ac B P 049 5 436 1735 M lat co), and best explains the rise of the others.tn Grk “conscious(ness) of God,” an awareness of God and allegiance to him.

verses.zh: 你们若因犯罪受责打，能忍耐，有甚么可夸的呢？但你们若因行善受苦，能忍耐，这在　神看是可喜爱的。
verses.en: For what credit is it if you sin and are mistreated and endure it? But if you do good and suffer and so endure, this finds favor with God.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “For this [is] favor/grace with God,” used as a metonymy as in vs. 19 of that which pleases him, which he looks on with favor (cf. BDAG 1079 s.v. χάρις 2).

verses.zh: 你们蒙召原是为此；因基督也为你们受过苦，给你们留下榜样，叫你们跟随他的脚踪行。
verses.en: For to this you were called, since Christ also suffered for you, leaving an example for you to follow in his steps.

verses.zh: 他并没有犯罪，口里也没有诡诈。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] committed no sin nor was deceit found in his mouth.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “who,” referring to Christ and applying the quotations from Isa 53 to him. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
A quotation from Isa 53:9.

verses.zh: 他被骂不还口；受害不说威吓的话，只将自己交托那按公义审判人的主。
verses.en: When he was maligned, he[NOTE:1] did not answer back; when he suffered, he threatened[NOTE:2] no retaliation,[NOTE:3] but committed himself to God[NOTE:4] who judges justly.
notes: Grk “who being maligned,” continuing the reference to Christ. Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Grk “he did not threaten, but.”
An allusion to Isa 53:7.
Grk “to the one”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他被挂在木头上，亲身担当了我们的罪，使我们既然在罪上死，就得以在义上活。因他受的鞭伤，你们便得了医治。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] himself bore our sins[NOTE:2] in his body on the tree, that we may cease from sinning[NOTE:3] and live for righteousness. By his[NOTE:4] wounds[NOTE:5] you were healed.[NOTE:6]
notes: Grk “who.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
A quotation from Isa 53:4, 12.

The verb ἀπογίνομαι (apoginomai) occurs only here in the NT. It can have a literal meaning (“to die”; L&N 74.27) and a figurative meaning (“to cease”; L&N 68.40). Because it is opposite the verb ζάω (zaō, “to live”), many argue that the meaning of the verb here must be “die” (so BDAG 108 s.v.), but even so literal death would not be in view. “In place of ἀποθνῃσκιεν, the common verb for ‘die,’ ἀπογινεθαι serves Peter as a euphemism, with the meaning ‘to be away’ or ‘to depart’” (J. R. Michaels, 1 Peter [WBC 49], 148). It is a metaphorical way to refer to the decisive separation from sin Jesus accomplished for believers through his death; the result is that believers “may cease from sinning.”
Grk “whose.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
Grk the singular: “wound”; “injury.”
A quotation from Isa 53:5.

verses.zh: 你们从前好像迷路的羊，如今却归到你们灵魂的牧人监督了。
verses.en: For you were going astray like sheep[NOTE:1] but now you have turned back to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.
notes: A quotation from Isa 53:6.
